name: Modular Kitchen

scope_options.label: Straight (single-wall) kitchen
scope_options.description: All base and wall cabinets run along one wall. Priced as one complete kitchen: carcasses, shutters, hinges, drawer channels, handles and fitting. Whether the countertop, sink, chimney, hob, accessories and civil, plumbing or electrical work are included differs between firms, so check each quote.

scope_options.label: L-shaped kitchen
scope_options.description: Cabinets run along two adjoining walls and meet at one corner. Priced as one complete kitchen. NoBroker's Pune price bands use an 8×6 ft L-shaped kitchen with 14 ft of workspace as the reference size.

scope_options.label: U-shaped kitchen
scope_options.description: Cabinets run along three walls, with two corners. Priced as one complete kitchen. NoBroker's Pune price bands use a 10×8×6 ft U-shaped kitchen with 24 ft of workspace as the reference size.

scope_options.label: Parallel (galley) kitchen
scope_options.description: Cabinets run along two facing walls with a walkway between them. Priced as one complete kitchen. NoBroker's Pune price bands use 12×5 ft on both walls, 24 ft of workspace, as the reference size.

materials.label: Particle board or MDF carcass
materials.description: Engineered boards made from wood particles (particle board) or wood fibres (MDF), used for cabinet boxes and shutters. Livspace lists MDF at ₹40–₹90 and particle board at ₹30–₹60 per sq ft of board; HomeLane gives ₹60–₹120 per sq ft for MDF. NoBroker describes its budget kitchen packages as particle board or MDF with laminates.

sources.title: MDF vs Particle Board Differences: Everything You Need to Know
sources.quote: MDF costs ₹40 – ₹90 per sq. ft., compared to particle board at ₹30 – ₹60 per sq. ft.

sources.title: Modern Modular Kitchen Cabinets Design for Stylish Homes
sources.quote: MDF is the least expensive, at INR 60-120 per sq. ft.

sources.title: Kitchen Interior Design Cost India| Modular kitchen price 2026
sources.quote: Budget packages (₹1.8-2.6L) are made of particle board or MDF with laminates, mid-range (₹2.7-3.8L) are made of BWR plywood with quality finishes.

materials.label: BWR plywood carcass
materials.description: Plywood bonded with boiling-water-resistant (BWR) adhesive, used for cabinet boxes. HomeLane and NoBroker both describe their mid-range kitchens as built with BWR plywood, and HomeLane's Pune guide recommends BWP or BWR plywood for Pune's humidity.

sources.title: Modern Modular Kitchen Cabinets Design for Stylish Homes
sources.quote: Mid-range kitchens priced at ₹2 lakh – ₹3.5 lakh include BWR plywood cabinets, high-quality laminates or acrylic finishes, and storage accessories.

sources.title: Kitchen Interior Design Cost India| Modular kitchen price 2026
sources.quote: Budget packages (₹1.8-2.6L) are made of particle board or MDF with laminates, mid-range (₹2.7-3.8L) are made of BWR plywood with quality finishes.

materials.label: BWP plywood carcass
materials.description: Plywood bonded with boiling-water-proof (BWP) adhesive, used for cabinet boxes. HomeLane says BWP or BWR plywood is used for the core because it resists moisture better than MDF or particle board. NoBroker gives ₹1,800–₹2,800 per sq ft for mid-range kitchens built in BWP plywood with laminate or membrane shutters.

sources.quote: BWP or BWR plywood is used for the core because it resists moisture better than MDF or particle board.

materials.label: HDHMR board
materials.description: HDHMR board, an engineered board offered for kitchen cabinets and furniture. HomeLane publishes an HDHMR guide for kitchen cabinets and home furniture, and Design Cafe one for home interiors; both were seen only as page titles, so no properties or prices are cited here. Ask the firm for the brand, thickness and grade quoted.

duration_days.basis: From design sign-off to handover for a standard kitchen. Design Cafe gives about 4–6 weeks (28–42 days) for design, factory manufacturing and installation, of which on-site installation is 4–7 days once plumbing, electrical and civil work are finished. HomeLane gives about 45 days for most standard projects from the first design conversation to handover. Civil changes, custom elements and site delays add time.

questions_to_ask: Is your price a lump sum for the whole kitchen, a rate per sq ft or a rate per running foot? If it is per sq ft, is that per sq ft of kitchen floor, cabinet front or shutter area, and what quantity did you measure?
Which board will you use for the carcasses and for the shutters, in which grade, thickness and brand, and is the sink unit made from a water-resistant grade such as BWP plywood?
Which shutter finish is quoted, what finish is on the inner face of the shutters, and how are the edges sealed?
Which brands of hinges, drawer channels, baskets and lift-up fittings are included, are they soft-close, and how many drawers and baskets does the quote cover?
Is the countertop included? If so, which stone, what thickness and edge profile, and are the sink and hob cut-outs included?
Are the sink, tap, chimney, hob, removal of the old platform, plumbing and electrical changes and dado tiling included, excluded or extra?
Will I get a measured drawing (2D or 3D) showing every cabinet's width, height and depth to sign off before production starts?
Will you re-measure on site after the plumbing, electrical and tiling work is finished?
What is the schedule from design sign-off to installation, and how are payments linked to stages?
What warranty do you give on the boards, the hardware and the workmanship, and will you put it in writing?
common_mistakes: Finalising cabinet sizes before choosing the chimney, hob, oven, dishwasher, refrigerator and water purifier, so appliances do not fit their spaces.
Letting the kitchen be measured for production before plumbing, electrical points and wall tiling are finished.
Accepting a moisture-sensitive board for the sink unit, where water from the tap, waste pipe and cleaning collects.
Comparing quotes that assume different boards, finishes or hardware brands as if they covered the same kitchen.
Comparing a rate per sq ft with a rate per running foot or a lump sum without converting all of them to a total for the same kitchen.
Comparing package prices without checking which ones include a chimney, hob, sink or other appliances.
Not planning corner units, so corner space is lost or drawers and handles clash when opened.
Not planning sockets for the chimney, microwave, mixer, water purifier and under-cabinet lights before tiling.
Paying most of the amount upfront instead of linking payments to design sign-off, delivery and installation.
quote_checklist: Price basis (lump sum, sq ft of a stated area, or running feet) and the measured quantity
Layout and a drawing showing every cabinet's width, height and depth
Carcass board: type, grade, thickness and brand
Shutter board and finish: type, brand, inner-face finish and edge sealing
Hardware: brands of hinges, drawer channels, baskets and lift-up fittings, whether soft-close, and the count of each
Countertop: material, thickness, edge profile, cut-outs and backsplash
Sink, tap, chimney, hob and other appliances: included, excluded or a stated allowance
Civil, plumbing and electrical work, removal of the old platform and dado tiling: included or extra
Handles, plinth or skirting and loft units: included or extra
Transport, installation and debris removal: included or extra
Schedule from design sign-off to installation, with a stage-wise payment plan
Written warranty on boards, hardware and workmanship
Whether GST is included or extra

faq.q: How much does a modular kitchen cost in Pune?
faq.a: It depends on the layout, the cabinet board and the shutter finish. Our draft cost models, built from publisher price guides retrieved in October 2026, give these ranges per kitchen: about ₹80,000–₹2.6 lakh for a budget laminate kitchen on particle board or MDF, ₹2–₹3.8 lakh for a standard BWR-plywood kitchen, and ₹2.5–₹7 lakh for a premium acrylic or PU kitchen. By layout, NoBroker's Pune guide gives ₹1.5–₹4.5 lakh for a straight kitchen, ₹2–₹5.5 lakh for an L-shaped kitchen and ₹2.8–₹7 lakh for a U-shaped kitchen. These are indicative ranges, not quotations.

faq.q: Why do per-sq-ft prices for modular kitchens differ so much?
faq.a: Publishers measure different areas. Livspace quotes ₹2,600–₹4,000 per sq ft of kitchen floor area for an 80–100 sq ft parallel kitchen. HomeLane gives ₹1,200–₹2,500 per sq ft for Pune and ₹700–₹900 per sq ft for a laminate finish. NoBroker quotes Pune base units at ₹4,000–₹8,000 per running foot. Ask every firm which area its rate uses, and compare the total for your kitchen.

faq.q: What might not be included in a modular kitchen quote?
faq.a: It differs between firms. NoBroker lists a basic chimney, hob and sink in its budget package, and HomeLane lists built-in appliances in its luxury kitchens, while other price guides do not say. HomeLane's Pune guide says basic accessories such as cutlery trays and soft-close hinges add ₹18,000–₹35,000. Ask for the countertop, sink and tap, appliances, accessories, removal of the old platform, plumbing and electrical changes and dado tiling to be marked included, excluded or extra.

faq.q: Which board should be used for the sink unit?
faq.a: The sink unit is exposed to water from the tap, the waste pipe, leaks and cleaning. HomeLane's Pune guide recommends BWP or BWR plywood for Pune's humidity. Ask which board and grade the sink unit uses, and check that cut edges and pipe openings are sealed.

faq.q: What is the difference between laminate, acrylic, membrane and PU shutters?
faq.a: Laminate is a decorative sheet pressed onto the board, in glossy, matte or textured surfaces. Acrylic is an acrylic sheet bonded to the board. Livspace describes membrane as PVC foil wrapped around MDF or HDF-HMR board under vacuum. PU is polyurethane paint applied over the board. HomeLane's guides put acrylic at roughly 15–30% and PU at roughly 30–45% above laminate; Design Cafe says acrylic can raise shutter-related costs by 15–30% over basic laminate. Ask to see a sample of the exact finish and colour quoted.

faq.q: How long does a modular kitchen take?
faq.a: Design Cafe gives about 4–6 weeks from design to installation, and HomeLane about 45 days for most standard projects. Design Cafe puts on-site installation at 4–7 days once plumbing, electrical and civil work are finished. Civil changes and custom elements add time, so ask for a written schedule with dates for design sign-off, delivery and installation.

faq.q: When should the kitchen be measured?
faq.a: Take the final measurement for production after plumbing, electrical points and wall tiling are finished, because these change the usable space. Ask the firm to re-measure on site and to confirm the drawing with you before production starts.

faq.q: Do I need to inform my housing society?
faq.a: Check with your society office before work starts. Ask about permitted working hours and any rules on noise, lift use and debris disposal, especially if the old platform has to be broken out.
